According to Bloomberg reports, OpenAI's first product entering the hardware market is expected to be a portable, screen-less smart speaker. Here are the details.

One of five products in development

Although OpenAI announced its entry into the hardware market as early as May 2025 together with Jony Ive's io Products, the project subsequently went quiet until Apple filed a trade secrets lawsuit, which brought renewed attention to the products OpenAI is developing.

Shortly after the initial announcement, another company called iyO filed a trademark infringement lawsuit against OpenAI and io Products, and the related court documents revealed for the first time what this project is "not": the first device in development is neither a wearable nor an in-ear product.

Now, Bloomberg has reported the device's true positioning. The report is as follows:

and

Popular comments posted by DHa

I don't find this product very appealing. I wouldn't want to carry my phone around, set it up, and then lug a device roughly the size of a HomePod everywhere I go.

The report states that the device can be plugged in and placed in one room for long-term use, but it also comes with a rechargeable battery that "allows users to carry it with them throughout the day as they move between different rooms":

The report also mentions that, although inevitable comparisons will be drawn with Apple's HomePod—especially given the heightened scrutiny amid Apple's trade secrets lawsuit—"OpenAI believes its first product has not infringed any trade secrets."

Finally, Bloomberg points out that this smart speaker is only one of roughly five products OpenAI currently has in development, and according to reports, the company's longer-term plans include "a mobile AI device that could replace the smartphone." At the same time, the company has also "explored wearable products, including pendant devices, and expressed interest in home robotics technology."
